title: A personal-loan enquiry at 9pm, qualified before the branch opens
scenario: Caller asks about a personal loan; the agent asks salary band, employer type and amount, explains the documents needed from the knowledge base, and books a branch callback.
hook: A customer wants a loan at 9pm, and the branch doesn't open till tomorrow.

title: A car accident claim, logged in Saudi Arabic in under two minutes
scenario: Caller had a minor collision; the agent takes policy number, date, location, whether anyone is hurt and the Najm report number, then gives a claim reference.
hook: The first call after a car accident decides whether a customer stays with you.

title: Ordering 10,000 litres of diesel for a construction site by phone
scenario: A site manager orders diesel; the agent confirms quantity, site location, delivery window and the account number, then reads the order back.
hook: A crane is idle because the site ran out of diesel.

title: A polite credit-card reminder call that never asks for a PIN
scenario: Outbound: the agent reminds a customer of the due date and minimum payment, offers the payment channels, and never asks for card numbers, PINs or OTPs.
hook: Collections calls are where banks lose customers, so here's one that doesn't.

title: Why is my bill higher this month? Answered at midnight
scenario: Caller disputes a higher bill; the agent explains roaming and add-on charges from the knowledge base and opens a review ticket if the caller still disagrees.
hook: Nobody calls a telecom company when they're happy.

title: Every business closes at 10pm. Its phone line doesn't have to
scenario: Caller rings after hours; the agent answers questions from the knowledge base, takes a message with name and number, and promises a morning callback.
hook: Half your calls come in when nobody's there to answer them.

title: A health-insurance quote request, qualified in Saudi Arabic
scenario: A small-business owner wants cover for 12 staff; the agent asks headcount, ages band and current insurer, and books a consultant call.
hook: A company with 12 staff wants health insurance tonight.

title: Booking a branch appointment for a mortgage, by voice
scenario: Caller wants to discuss a home loan; the agent checks which branch, offers two slots, and confirms by name and mobile.
hook: Mortgage customers want a person, and the first thing they want is an appointment.

title: A fuel-station complaint, routed to the right regional manager
scenario: A driver complains about a closed pump and a rude attendant; the agent logs station, time and issue, calms the caller, and escalates to the region.
hook: One bad fuel stop is enough to lose a fleet customer.

title: The appointment reminder that stops no-shows
scenario: Outbound: the agent reminds a patient of tomorrow's appointment, confirms or reschedules, and updates the booking.
hook: Every no-show is an empty chair you still pay for.

title: A bank switchboard that routes calls in Saudi Arabic
scenario: Caller asks for cards, loans or a branch; the agent asks one question, understands the dialect, and routes to the right team.
hook: Press 1 for cards is where customers hang up.

title: Where is my order? answered without a human
scenario: Caller asks about a late order; the agent looks up the order status via a function and gives the delivery date.
hook: Where is my order is the most asked question in retail.

title: A renewal reminder call before the policy lapses
scenario: Outbound: the agent reminds a customer their motor policy ends in 7 days and offers to book a renewal callback.
hook: A lapsed policy is a customer you already lost.

title: A government service line that understands Najdi and Hijazi
scenario: Caller asks how to renew an iqama-related document; the agent answers the steps from the knowledge base and points to the right channel.
hook: Government hotlines are where the waiting music never ends.

title: Ordering gas cylinders to your door in Saudi Arabic
scenario: A household orders two gas cylinders; the agent confirms the district, gate, and payment on delivery, and gives an arrival window.
hook: The gas runs out in the middle of cooking dinner.

title: A two-question survey after every branch visit
scenario: Outbound: the agent asks for a 1-to-5 rating and one reason, thanks the customer, and flags low scores.
hook: Banks send surveys by SMS, and nobody answers them.

title: Rebooking a missed flight in Saudi Arabic, at 3am
scenario: A passenger missed a connection; the agent explains rebooking options from the knowledge base and hands the case to the ops desk with the booking reference.
hook: You missed your flight, and it's three in the morning.

title: Screening 200 job applicants by phone in one afternoon
scenario: Outbound: the agent asks each applicant three screening questions, notes answers, and books interviews for the ones who fit.
hook: Two hundred people applied, and you have one afternoon.

title: A claim complaint handled calmly, then escalated
scenario: A customer is angry about a delayed claim; the agent acknowledges, gives the status, and escalates with a summary.
hook: Angry claim calls are the ones your team avoids.

title: A supplier hotline for a refinery: invoices, gate passes, tenders
scenario: A vendor asks about an unpaid invoice; the agent collects the invoice number and routes to accounts payable with a summary.
hook: Refinery suppliers spend hours on hold just to ask about an invoice.

title: Turning a credit-card ad into qualified leads by phone
scenario: Outbound: the agent calls people who clicked an ad, checks eligibility questions, and books a callback with sales.
hook: Most leads from a card ad are never called back.

title: A restaurant that takes bookings while the kitchen is slammed
scenario: Caller books a table for six on Thursday; the agent checks the time, takes the name, and confirms.
hook: The phone rings during the dinner rush, and nobody can answer it.

title: Selling a fibre upgrade by phone without a call center
scenario: Outbound: the agent offers a fibre upgrade to existing customers, answers speed and price questions, and books installation.
hook: Upgrades are the cheapest sale a telecom company can make.

title: A home water-leak claim, logged at 2am
scenario: Caller has a burst pipe; the agent logs the address, damage and photos-to-send instructions, and gives emergency contractor info from the knowledge base.
hook: Pipes burst at night, never during office hours.

title: A disputed card transaction, logged without asking for the PIN
scenario: Caller doesn't recognise a charge; the agent records amount, date and merchant, never asks for PIN or OTP, and opens a dispute case.
hook: Here's how a bank's AI should handle fraud calls, and what it must never ask.

title: A courier that reschedules deliveries by voice
scenario: Caller won't be home; the agent reschedules delivery to tomorrow afternoon and confirms the address.
hook: Missed deliveries cost couriers twice.

title: Screening field technicians for a rig contract
scenario: Outbound: the agent asks certification, years on rigs and availability, and shortlists candidates.
hook: An oil contractor needs thirty technicians by next month.

title: A hospital switchboard that finds the right department
scenario: Caller asks for cardiology results; the agent routes to the department and never gives medical advice.
hook: Hospital switchboards are the busiest phone lines in the city.

title: A bank hotline that answers fee questions at midnight
scenario: Caller asks about transfer fees and limits; the agent answers from the knowledge base and offers a callback for anything account-specific.
hook: Customers don't have banking questions only between nine and five.

title: A return request handled in one call
scenario: Caller wants to return shoes; the agent explains the return policy, logs the order number, and books a pickup.
hook: Returns are where online shops lose repeat customers.

title: Travel insurance sold on the phone before the flight
scenario: Caller needs travel cover for a family of four; the agent asks destination and dates and books a quote callback.
hook: The family flies on Friday and needs insurance by Thursday.

title: A power-outage line that tells you what's happening
scenario: Caller reports an outage; the agent logs the district, checks known outages from the knowledge base, and gives an estimate.
hook: When the power goes out, everyone calls at once.

title: Booking a car service by voice, in Saudi Arabic
scenario: Caller needs a 20,000 km service; the agent offers two slots and confirms car model and plate.
hook: Car owners hate calling the service center.

title: A loan instalment reminder that people actually thank you for
scenario: Outbound: the agent reminds of an instalment due in three days and offers payment channels, no personal data asked.
hook: Nobody likes a debt reminder, unless it sounds like this.

title: An HSE incident hotline that never goes to voicemail
scenario: A contractor reports a minor spill; the agent logs site, time, substance and injuries, and escalates immediately.
hook: On an oil site, a safety report can't wait for Monday.

title: A no-internet complaint, triaged in one call
scenario: Caller has no internet; the agent walks through a router restart from the knowledge base, then opens a technician ticket.
hook: No internet is the call every telecom company dreads.

title: A claims survey that catches unhappy customers before they leave
scenario: Outbound after a closed claim: the agent asks two questions and flags anyone scoring under 3.
hook: The time to save a customer is right after their claim.

title: A municipality line that takes reports at night
scenario: Caller reports a broken streetlight; the agent logs the location and gives a reference number.
hook: Broken streetlights get reported at night, when they matter.

title: A corporate-banking desk that screens calls for relationship managers
scenario: A business client calls; the agent takes the company name and request and routes to the right relationship manager.
hook: Relationship managers spend half their day on calls that aren't for them.

title: Selling off-plan apartments by phone to overseas buyers
scenario: Caller asks about off-plan units; the agent gives payment plans from the knowledge base and books a video viewing.
hook: An investor in London wants to buy in Riyadh.

title: Lubricant distributor orders, taken by an AI desk
scenario: A workshop orders engine oil; the agent confirms products, quantities and delivery date.
hook: Workshops reorder oil every week, by phone.

title: A hotel front desk that answers in Arabic and English
scenario: A guest asks about late checkout and airport transfer; the agent answers from the knowledge base and books the transfer.
hook: Hotel front desks answer the same ten questions all day.

title: Qualifying SME finance leads for a bank
scenario: A shop owner asks about business finance; the agent asks turnover, years trading and need, and books an advisor.
hook: Small businesses want finance, and banks want to know who qualifies.

title: A medical claim reimbursement, started by voice
scenario: Caller wants to claim a clinic visit; the agent explains the documents needed and logs the case.
hook: Medical claims start with confusion about paperwork.

title: A freight company qualifying shipping leads by phone
scenario: Caller wants to ship containers; the agent asks route, volume and timing, then books a sales call.
hook: Freight quotes are lost when nobody answers fast.

title: A pharmacy line that answers stock questions at night
scenario: Caller asks whether a medicine is in stock; the agent checks the knowledge base list and never gives dosage advice.
hook: Pharmacies get asked the same stock question all night.

title: A call-center quality check by the AI itself
scenario: Outbound: the agent calls customers who spoke to support today and asks whether their issue was solved.
hook: The best quality check is asking the customer, the same day.

title: A fuel-card support line for fleet managers
scenario: A fleet manager's card is blocked; the agent logs the card's last digits, never full numbers, and routes to support.
hook: A blocked fuel card stops a whole fleet.

title: A furniture store qualifying delivery-and-assembly leads
scenario: Caller asks about a sofa and delivery; the agent answers price from the knowledge base and books assembly.
hook: Big-ticket buyers call before they buy.

title: An insurance switchboard: claims, sales or renewals in one question
scenario: Caller is routed after one question, in dialect.
hook: Insurance callers don't know which department they need.

title: A prepaid top-up reminder that keeps customers connected
scenario: Outbound: the agent reminds a customer their package ends tomorrow and explains how to renew.
hook: Customers churn when their package quietly runs out.

title: A car dealership that follows up every test-drive lead
scenario: Outbound: the agent calls test-drive leads, asks budget and timeline, and books a showroom visit.
hook: Car dealers lose leads they never called back.

title: A lost-card call at 2am: blocked-card steps, and what the AI must not ask
scenario: Caller lost a card; the agent explains how to freeze it in the app, routes to the emergency line, and never asks for card details.
hook: Losing your card at 2am is the worst banking call there is.

title: A B2B fuel-delivery survey after every drop
scenario: Outbound: the agent asks the site manager whether the delivery was on time and complete.
hook: Fuel customers leave when deliveries run late, not when prices rise.

title: A water bill question answered from the tariff table
scenario: Caller asks why the bill doubled; the agent explains the tariff tiers from the knowledge base.
hook: Water bills make people angry because nobody explains them.

title: A travel agency qualifying Umrah package enquiries
scenario: Caller asks about Umrah packages; the agent asks dates and group size and books a consultant.
hook: Umrah season means every travel agency phone rings at once.

title: A civil-affairs appointment booked by voice
scenario: Caller books an appointment; the agent offers slots and confirms by ID-free details (name and mobile only).
hook: Booking a government appointment shouldn't take an hour.

title: Chasing unpaid premiums without damaging the relationship
scenario: Outbound: the agent reminds a small business of an unpaid premium and books a callback.
hook: Premium collections are awkward, so let the AI be polite about it.

title: One AI, ten bank branches: which branch is open on Saturday?
scenario: Caller asks branch hours and location; the agent answers from the knowledge base for every branch.
hook: The most common bank call is where and when.

title: Every missed call is a missed sale: an AI that calls leads back in 60 seconds
scenario: Outbound 'Call new leads instantly': the agent calls a web lead within a minute and qualifies them.
hook: Leads go cold in five minutes, so this calls them back in one.
